editorial:
Imagine stepping back in time to a cozy home in St. Louis right before the 1904 World's Fair. You get to meet the Smith family, a group of lovable people dealing with the scary thought of moving away from their hometown. The whole vibe is warm and fuzzy, filled with young love, funny family fights, and a lot of singing. It feels like a giant hug in movie form, especially with the holiday setting. You will find yourself rooting for the kids to find love and for the parents to make the right choice for the family.

What really makes this version special is how it was put together during the pandemic. Even though it was filmed remotely, the passion for the music shines through. The songs like The Trolley Song are absolute treats that will get stuck in your head. While the abridged length means some plot points move fast, it keeps the energy high. It is a perfect pick for a family movie night where you just want to feel happy.
endingExplained: Everything wraps up with the family deciding to stay in St. Louis after all. The tension over moving away disappears once the parents realize how much the city means to them. The romantic couples finally get together, and the holiday spirit wins. You see the family reunited and happy, looking forward to the excitement of the World's Fair. It ends on a high note with a feeling of peace and togetherness for everyone involved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic musicals and heartwarming holiday stories.
